comparison: Both strongly support the Apollo Implant design specifications (C5-C92 in OpenEval; overlapping claims in peer review). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of measurements and costs from Table 1 and Figure 1. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the lightweight, customizable design and open-source nature. High agreement on design features, though OpenEval covers more granular technical claims (C67, C74, C82-C85 not in peer review).

Both strongly support multi-lab validation (C14-C99). OpenEval documents specific animal counts and experimental conditions across labs. Peer reviewers explicitly praise validation across 8 labs, multiple species, and experimental conditions as a major strength. Very high agreement, with peer review also incorporating success rate claims (C133, C234, C245-C247) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Both support recording stability claims (C18-C126 in OpenEval; overlapping in peer review). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis but notes qualifications (3% daily decline, high variability). Peer Reviewer 1 finds validation analyses 'very convincing.' Peer review also incorporates RMS stability claims (C135-C138, C141) that OpenEval addresses separately in R5. Agreement on overall stability despite OpenEval noting more nuanced limitations.

Both support statistical findings about recording stability (C127-C132). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of linear mixed-effects models with p-values, noting posterior variability claims are more qualitative. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of 'very convincing' validation analyses without explicit discussion. Also includes RMS claims (C139-C140) that overlap with OpenEval R5.

Partial overlap on RMS and amplitude stability (C135-C141). OpenEval R5 focuses specifically on quantitative RMS/amplitude analyses from Figure 4G-L. Peer R3 incorporates these claims within broader recording stability evaluation. Both support the findings, though OpenEval notes the biological significance of AP position effect is not fully explored.

Minor overlap on RMS claims (C139-C140). OpenEval R5 addresses these as part of comprehensive RMS/amplitude stability analysis. Peer R4 includes them with statistical findings about recording stability. Both support these specific claims.

Both support neuron tracking findings (C142-C158). OpenEval documents 50% same-day matching ceiling and high variability (0-20% at different timepoints), appropriately acknowledging methodological limitations. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly affirms tracking capability as 'critical for a large number of experiments.' Agreement on tracking success with OpenEval providing more detailed quantitative assessment of variability.

Perfect claim overlap on freely moving recordings (C159-C171). Both strongly support these findings. OpenEval notes quantitative RMS/amplitude comparisons but observes that movement impairment claims are based on qualitative rather than systematic behavioral quantification. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm successful freely moving recordings across labs and conditions. High agreement with OpenEval providing more methodological scrutiny.

Both support behavioral task performance claims (C172-C183). OpenEval documents recovery of hit rate and trial number but notes persistent reaction time elevation and small sample size (n=2) as limitations. Peer Reviewer 2 states animals 'can even perform complex behavioral tasks, with no apparent reduction in their performance.' Agreement on overall capability, though OpenEval emphasizes limitations more explicitly than peer review.

Both support explantation and recovery rate claims (C235-C247). OpenEval documents distinction between physical damage and connection errors, with high success rates in secondary labs. Peer reviewers implicitly accept probe reusability as demonstrated, with Reviewer 2 explicitly praising ability to 'explant and reuse' probes. Strong agreement on recovery rates and reusability.

Minor overlap on secondary lab success rates (C245-C247). OpenEval R9 addresses these as evidence for ease of use in explantation context. Peer R2 incorporates them as part of broader multi-lab validation success. Both support these claims.

Partial overlap on design advantages and comparisons (C184-C234 in OpenEval; C185-C188, C201-C206 in peer review). OpenEval provides comprehensive discussion of advantages with citations and quantitative comparisons, noting some claims are speculative. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm weight, cost, and open-source advantages. Agreement on documented advantages, with OpenEval covering broader discussion claims.

Minor overlap on behavioral impact discussion (C199, C211). OpenEval R10 includes these as part of broader discussion context. Peer R7 addresses behavioral performance more directly through experimental data. Both support overall suitability for behavioral experiments.

Minimal overlap on single claim C228 about neuron tracking advantages. OpenEval R10 includes this as part of discussion context. Peer R5 focuses on tracking methodology and results. Both support tracking capability.

Minimal overlap on claim C234 about multi-lab success. OpenEval R10 includes this as discussion point about validation. Peer R2 addresses multi-lab validation comprehensively. Both strongly support this claim.

Both support background and context claims (C1-C42 in OpenEval; overlapping subset in peer review). OpenEval documents these as established knowledge with appropriate citations framing the study motivation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as standard field understanding. Complete agreement on background context.

Overlap on limitations of existing devices (C30-C32, C40-C42). OpenEval R11 presents these as background context supported by citations. Peer R9 explicitly affirms these limitations, with Reviewer 2 stating previous devices 'hampered' chronic use. Strong agreement that Apollo addresses previous device limitations.

OpenEval R12 addresses practical advantages of chronic implants (C105-C108) including efficiency claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found that specifically addresses these claims, though they are implicitly accepted as part of overall design advantages discussed in peer R1.

OpenEval R13 addresses practical advantages of probe bank switching and neuron tracking potential (C48-C50). No corresponding peer review evaluation found that specifically addresses these claims as a distinct group, though related concepts are discussed in peer reviews of design features and tracking results.

OpenEval R14 addresses speculative claim C134 about tissue response, appropriately marking it as UNCERTAIN with limited evidence (one mouse, anecdotal). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. This represents preliminary findings rather than established conclusions.

Minimal overlap on single claim C133 about statistical analysis. OpenEval R4 addresses this as part of linear mixed-effects model results. Peer R2 incorporates it within multi-lab validation context. Both support the statistical approach.
